b. security officers; and/or

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Point a What is meant by Gender Responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and be able to empower victims. Point b Sufficiently clear Point c What is meant by equal and respectful relationships is that whoever the victim, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing beliefs, values and social status.
Point d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only by people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims. Point e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that officers providing services must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems. Point f What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (Coping mechanism) so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any matter.

HEAD OF LEGAL DIVISION,
DEWA PUTU OKA, S.H. NIP. 19750815 200212 1 004
ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION OF SUKAMARA REGENCY
NUMBER 9 OF 2022
CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
1. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution as a Constitutional foundation has explicitly regulated the importance of protection of Human Rights, including the rights of women and children. In addition to the guarantee from the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the guarantee that every person must have equal dignity and degree has also been recognized internationally. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights or UDHR of 1948 which underlies Human Rights in general has guaranteed that all people are born with freedom, having equal dignity and rights without exception.

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and manage regional government affairs aimed at realizing community welfare through improved services, protection and empowerment of the community. As a community component that plays an important role in realizing a quality generation and as successors to the nation's struggle, women and children must receive guarantees for the fulfillment of children's rights.

To ensure the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in accordance with human dignity and in order to carry out mandatory affairs, regional governments need to provide legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection through the formulation of a policy. The formulation of such policy is a form of support and concrete effort from various other parties in ensuring the fulfillment of the rights of women and children.

The Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is carried out based on the principles of:
a. non-discrimination;
b. the best interests of women and children;
c. the right to life, survival and development; d. respect for children and legal certainty; and
e. local wisdom and justice and gender equality.

The formulation of the Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to:
a. provide guidance in planning and implementing Women's Empowerment and Child Protection policies;
b. increase efforts for Women's Empowerment and fulfillment of children's rights in order to realize improved quality of life for women and children in the Region;
c. increase protection efforts for women and children from actions and policies that violate the rights of women and children; d. increase the value of local wisdom and the role of customs in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, and
e. increase the role of Regional Government and other community institutions in efforts for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation on Women and Child Protection regulates:
a. Improvement of women's quality of life which contains government responsibilities, implementation of PUG, Efforts to increase the role, quality and capacity of women in the political, legal, social and economic fields;
b. Protection of women which contains regional government responsibilities in women's protection, prevention of violence against women, protection for women victims of violence, as well as complaint handling,
c. Child Protection which contains the responsibilities of regional government, parents/family and community in child protection as well as efforts made by regional governments in implementing child protection. In addition, the need to establish a children's forum and Child-Friendly Regency as a form of appreciation in realizing protection and fulfillment of children's rights.

Article 20
Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Point a What is meant by Gender Responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and be able to empower victims. Point b Sufficiently clear Point c What is meant by equal and respectful relationships is that whoever the victim, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing beliefs, values and social status.
Point d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only by people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims. Point e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that officers providing services must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems. Point f What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (Coping mechanism) so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any matter.
Point g What is meant by non-judgmental is that officers providing services must ensure that whatever the victim's condition, they will not be assessed or judged.
Point h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the victim will not be assessed or judged Point i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers, it must be ensured that victims are served in language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled/difable/disable women have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those experiencing mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided, for example from special education school teachers.
Point j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to be able to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter and efforts must be made so that the victim is not asked repeatedly about the same things related to identity or case narrative Point k What is meant by empathy, namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problems Point l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination and participation.
As regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child (Convention on the Rights of Child) and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Discrimination Against Women).

Article 31
(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services are intended to provide assistance and protection to women victims of acts of violence and sanctions with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and legal certainty.
(2) Types of legal aid services include:
a. legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of official investigation reports;
b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal aid in the examination process at court; d. legal aid in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision; and
e. legal aid in the mediation process.

Article 51
(1) Every organizer of an educational unit is obligated to provide opportunities for children to obtain services without discrimination.

(3) In the event that a child victim of violence experiences dropping out of school, the organizer of the educational unit is obligated to coordinate with related agencies.

Article 76

Article 51
Paragraph (1) What is meant by children with special needs are children who experience limitations/exceptionalities whether physical, mental, intellectual, social, or emotional that significantly influence the process of growth and development compared to other children of the same age.

Article 1

3. Regent is the Regent of Sukamara.

5. Women's Empowerment is an effort to empower women to obtain access and control over economic, political and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept.
6. Women's Protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination both in the form of preventive, repressive and postremedial protection (assistance and treatment).
7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children who are still in the womb and are not married.
9. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children.
10. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
11. Children's forum is a forum for children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitments and resources, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.
13. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social.
14. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual and social needs of citizens so that they can live properly and are able to develop themselves so that they can carry out their social functions.
15. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or outside the Country.
20. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community.
21. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
22. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations.
23. PUG focal point is an OPD operator who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.
24. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that are gender sensitive.
25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving Region to the region of origin.
26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide a sense of security to victims of violence.
28. Transit house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children so that they can grow and develop properly.
29. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche and systematic towards the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
30. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
31. Gender Sensitivity or gender awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men and the experience that problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different.
32. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on law for public service activities and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities.
33. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women and children from various fields of development as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including human trafficking formed by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, science and technology information centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), transit houses, children's friend telephone (TESSA) 129 or other forms.
34. Community organization is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila.
35. Parents are biological father and/or mother or stepfather and/or stepmother or adoptive father and/or mother.
36. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
37. Customs are local wisdom values that apply and are still applied from generation to generation in the community environment.
38. Regency Task Force is a coordination body at the regency level that coordinates policy efforts, programs and activities to realize a child-friendly regency.
39. Action plan is the Regional Development of Child-Friendly Regency is a document containing policies, programs and activities to realize a Child-Friendly Regency.

(1) Spiritual guidance as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (2) letter c aims for psychological recovery.

Article 28
(1) Regional Government may provide safe houses for women victims of acts of violence.

12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitments and resources, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

14. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual and social needs of citizens so that they can live properly and are able to develop themselves so that they can carry out their social functions.

16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.

18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or outside the Country.
20. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community.
21. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
22. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations.

24. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that are gender sensitive.
25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving Region to the region of origin.
26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide a sense of security to victims of violence.
28. Transit house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children so that they can grow and develop properly.
29. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche and systematic towards the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
30. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
31. Gender Sensitivity or gender awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men and the experience that problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different.
32. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on law for public service activities and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities.
33. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women and children from various fields of development as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including human trafficking formed by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, science and technology information centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), transit houses, children's friend telephone (TESSA) 129 or other forms.
34. Community organization is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila.
35. Parents are biological father and/or mother or stepfather and/or stepmother or adoptive father and/or mother.
36. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
37. Customs are local wisdom values that apply and are still applied from generation to generation in the community environment.

39. Action plan is the Regional Development of Child-Friendly Regency is a document containing policies, programs and activities to realize a Child-Friendly Regency.

Article 63
(1) Every person/entity is prohibited from employing and involving children in the worst forms of work.

d. all work that endangers the health, safety or morals of children.

5. Women's Empowerment is an effort to empower women to obtain access and control over economic, political and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept.
6. Women's Protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination both in the form of preventive, repressive and postremedial protection (assistance and treatment).
7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children who are still in the womb and are not married.
9. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children.
10. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
11. Children's forum is a forum for children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitments and resources, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.
13. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social.
14. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual and social needs of citizens so that they can live properly and are able to develop themselves so that they can carry out their social functions.
15. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or outside the Country.
20. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community.
21. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
22. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations.
23. PUG focal point is an OPD operator who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.
24. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that are gender sensitive.
25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving Region to the region of origin.
26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide a sense of security to victims of violence.
28. Transit house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children so that they can grow and develop properly.
29. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche and systematic towards the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
30. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
31. Gender Sensitivity or gender awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men and the experience that problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different.
32. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on law for public service activities and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities.
33. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women and children from various fields of development as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including human trafficking formed by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, science and technology information centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), transit houses, children's friend telephone (TESSA) 129 or other forms.
34. Community organization is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila.
35. Parents are biological father and/or mother or stepfather and/or stepmother or adoptive father and/or mother.
36. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
37. Customs are local wisdom values that apply and are still applied from generation to generation in the community environment.

39. Action plan is the Regional Development of Child-Friendly Regency is a document containing policies, programs and activities to realize a Child-Friendly Regency.

Article 29
(1) Spiritual guidance as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (2) letter c aims for psychological recovery.
(2) Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented based on the principles of:
a. not imposing any religion or belief; and
b. leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim.
(3) Spiritual guidance is conducted by spiritual guidance officers.
(4) Spiritual guidance officers as referred to in paragraph (3) consist of consultants from the Marriage Advisory, Development and Preservation Board, Officers of the Religious Affairs Office, religious leaders, who possess gender sensitivity or gender awareness.

Article 26
(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 22 letter c, is intended to restore and develop the capabilities of women victims of violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services:
a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
(3) The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by:
a. PD that administers governmental affairs in the social sector;
b. PD that administers governmental affairs in the sector of women and child empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers women crisis center or social community organizations that already exist; or
c. religious institutions and/or organizations.

Article 51
(1) Every organizer of an educational unit is obligated to provide opportunities for children to obtain services without discrimination.
(2) Every organizer of an educational unit is prohibited from expelling children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the child's education.
(3) In the event that a child victim of violence experiences dropping out of school, the organizer of the educational unit is obligated to coordinate with related agencies.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Sukamara Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sukamara.
4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Sukamara Regency Government.
5. Women's Empowerment is an effort to empower women to obtain access and control over economic, political and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept.
6. Women's Protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination both in the form of preventive, repressive and postremedial protection (assistance and treatment).
7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children who are still in the womb and are not married.
9. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children.
10. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
11. Children's forum is a forum for children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitments and resources, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.
13. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social.
14. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual and social needs of citizens so that they can live properly and are able to develop themselves so that they can carry out their social functions.
15. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or outside the Country.
20. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community.
21. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
22. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations.
23. PUG focal point is an OPD operator who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.
24. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that are gender sensitive.
25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving Region to the region of origin.
26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide a sense of security to victims of violence.
28. Transit house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children so that they can grow and develop properly.
29. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche and systematic towards the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
30. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
31. Gender Sensitivity or gender awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men and the experience that problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different.
32. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on law for public service activities and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities.
33. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women and children from various fields of development as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including human trafficking formed by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, science and technology information centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), transit houses, children's friend telephone (TESSA) 129 or other forms.
34. Community organization is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila.
35. Parents are biological father and/or mother or stepfather and/or stepmother or adoptive father and/or mother.
36. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
37. Customs are local wisdom values that apply and are still applied from generation to generation in the community environment.
38. Regency Task Force is a coordination body at the regency level that coordinates policy efforts, programs and activities to realize a child-friendly regency.
39. Action plan is the Regional Development of Child-Friendly Regency is a document containing policies, programs and activities to realize a Child-Friendly Regency.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Sukamara Regency.

3. Regent is the Regent of Sukamara.
4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Sukamara Regency Government.
5. Women's Empowerment is an effort to empower women to obtain access and control over economic, political and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept.
6. Women's Protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination both in the form of preventive, repressive and postremedial protection (assistance and treatment).
7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children who are still in the womb and are not married.
9. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children.
10. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
11. Children's forum is a forum for children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitments and resources, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.
13. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social.
14. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual and social needs of citizens so that they can live properly and are able to develop themselves so that they can carry out their social functions.
15. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or outside the Country.
20. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community.
21. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
22. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations.
23. PUG focal point is an OPD operator who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.
24. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that are gender sensitive.
25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving Region to the region of origin.
26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide a sense of security to victims of violence.
28. Transit house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children so that they can grow and develop properly.
29. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche and systematic towards the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
30. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
31. Gender Sensitivity or gender awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men and the experience that problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different.
32. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on law for public service activities and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities.
33. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women and children from various fields of development as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including human trafficking formed by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, science and technology information centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), transit houses, children's friend telephone (TESSA) 129 or other forms.
34. Community organization is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila.
35. Parents are biological father and/or mother or stepfather and/or stepmother or adoptive father and/or mother.
36. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
37. Customs are local wisdom values that apply and are still applied from generation to generation in the community environment.
38. Regency Task Force is a coordination body at the regency level that coordinates policy efforts, programs and activities to realize a child-friendly regency.
39. Action plan is the Regional Development of Child-Friendly Regency is a document containing policies, programs and activities to realize a Child-Friendly Regency.

Article 31
(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services are intended to provide assistance and protection to women victims of acts of violence and sanctions with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and legal certainty.
(2) Types of legal aid services include:
a. legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of official investigation reports;
b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal aid in the examination process at court; d. legal aid in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision; and
e. legal aid in the mediation process.
(3) The Regional Government provides legal aid to women victims of acts of violence based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
(4) In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3), the Regional Government may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other legal assistants who are gender sensitive.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Sukamara Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sukamara.
4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Sukamara Regency Government.
5. Women's Empowerment is an effort to empower women to obtain access and control over economic, political and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept.
6. Women's Protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination both in the form of preventive, repressive and postremedial protection (assistance and treatment).
7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children who are still in the womb and are not married.
9. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children.
10. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
11. Children's forum is a forum for children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitments and resources, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.
13. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social.
14. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual and social needs of citizens so that they can live properly and are able to develop themselves so that they can carry out their social functions.
15. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or outside the Country.
20. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community.
21. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
22. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations.
23. PUG focal point is an OPD operator who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.
24. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that are gender sensitive.
25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving Region to the region of origin.
26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide a sense of security to victims of violence.
28. Transit house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children so that they can grow and develop properly.
29. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche and systematic towards the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
30. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
31. Gender Sensitivity or gender awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men and the experience that problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different.
32. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on law for public service activities and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities.
33. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women and children from various fields of development as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including human trafficking formed by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, science and technology information centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), transit houses, children's friend telephone (TESSA) 129 or other forms.
34. Community organization is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila.
35. Parents are biological father and/or mother or stepfather and/or stepmother or adoptive father and/or mother.
36. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
37. Customs are local wisdom values that apply and are still applied from generation to generation in the community environment.
38. Regency Task Force is a coordination body at the regency level that coordinates policy efforts, programs and activities to realize a child-friendly regency.
39. Action plan is the Regional Development of Child-Friendly Regency is a document containing policies, programs and activities to realize a Child-Friendly Regency.

CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
1. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution as a Constitutional foundation has explicitly regulated the importance of protection of Human Rights, including the rights of women and children. In addition to the guarantee from the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the guarantee that every person must have equal dignity and degree has also been recognized internationally. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights or UDHR of 1948 which underlies Human Rights in general has guaranteed that all people are born with freedom, having equal dignity and rights without exception.

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and manage regional government affairs aimed at realizing community welfare through improved services, protection and empowerment of the community. As a community component that plays an important role in realizing a quality generation and as successors to the nation's struggle, women and children must receive guarantees for the fulfillment of children's rights.

To ensure the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in accordance with human dignity and in order to carry out mandatory affairs, regional governments need to provide legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection through the formulation of a policy. The formulation of such policy is a form of support and concrete effort from various other parties in ensuring the fulfillment of the rights of women and children.

The Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is carried out based on the principles of:
a. non-discrimination;
b. the best interests of women and children;
c. the right to life, survival and development; d. respect for children and legal certainty; and
e. local wisdom and justice and gender equality.

The formulation of the Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to:
a. provide guidance in planning and implementing Women's Empowerment and Child Protection policies;
b. increase efforts for Women's Empowerment and fulfillment of children's rights in order to realize improved quality of life for women and children in the Region;
c. increase protection efforts for women and children from actions and policies that violate the rights of women and children; d. increase the value of local wisdom and the role of customs in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, and
e. increase the role of Regional Government and other community institutions in efforts for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation on Women and Child Protection regulates:
a. Improvement of women's quality of life which contains government responsibilities, implementation of PUG, Efforts to increase the role, quality and capacity of women in the political, legal, social and economic fields;
b. Protection of women which contains regional government responsibilities in women's protection, prevention of violence against women, protection for women victims of violence, as well as complaint handling,
c. Child Protection which contains the responsibilities of regional government, parents/family and community in child protection as well as efforts made by regional governments in implementing child protection. In addition, the need to establish a children's forum and Child-Friendly Regency as a form of appreciation in realizing protection and fulfillment of children's rights.

Article 20
Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Point a What is meant by Gender Responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and be able to empower victims. Point b Sufficiently clear Point c What is meant by equal and respectful relationships is that whoever the victim, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing beliefs, values and social status.
Point d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only by people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims. Point e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that officers providing services must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems. Point f What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (Coping mechanism) so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any matter.
Point g What is meant by non-judgmental is that officers providing services must ensure that whatever the victim's condition, they will not be assessed or judged.
Point h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the victim will not be assessed or judged Point i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers, it must be ensured that victims are served in language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled/difable/disable women have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those experiencing mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided, for example from special education school teachers.
Point j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to be able to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter and efforts must be made so that the victim is not asked repeatedly about the same things related to identity or case narrative Point k What is meant by empathy, namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problems Point l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination and participation.

DEWA PUTU OKA, S.H. NIP. 19750815 200212 1 004
ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION OF SUKAMARA REGENCY
NUMBER 9 OF 2022
CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
1. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution as a Constitutional foundation has explicitly regulated the importance of protection of Human Rights, including the rights of women and children. In addition to the guarantee from the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the guarantee that every person must have equal dignity and degree has also been recognized internationally. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights or UDHR of 1948 which underlies Human Rights in general has guaranteed that all people are born with freedom, having equal dignity and rights without exception.

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and manage regional government affairs aimed at realizing community welfare through improved services, protection and empowerment of the community. As a community component that plays an important role in realizing a quality generation and as successors to the nation's struggle, women and children must receive guarantees for the fulfillment of children's rights.

To ensure the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in accordance with human dignity and in order to carry out mandatory affairs, regional governments need to provide legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection through the formulation of a policy. The formulation of such policy is a form of support and concrete effort from various other parties in ensuring the fulfillment of the rights of women and children.

The Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is carried out based on the principles of:
a. non-discrimination;
b. the best interests of women and children;
c. the right to life, survival and development; d. respect for children and legal certainty; and
e. local wisdom and justice and gender equality.

The formulation of the Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to:
a. provide guidance in planning and implementing Women's Empowerment and Child Protection policies;
b. increase efforts for Women's Empowerment and fulfillment of children's rights in order to realize improved quality of life for women and children in the Region;
c. increase protection efforts for women and children from actions and policies that violate the rights of women and children; d. increase the value of local wisdom and the role of customs in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, and
e. increase the role of Regional Government and other community institutions in efforts for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation on Women and Child Protection regulates:
a. Improvement of women's quality of life which contains government responsibilities, implementation of PUG, Efforts to increase the role, quality and capacity of women in the political, legal, social and economic fields;
b. Protection of women which contains regional government responsibilities in women's protection, prevention of violence against women, protection for women victims of violence, as well as complaint handling,
c. Child Protection which contains the responsibilities of regional government, parents/family and community in child protection as well as efforts made by regional governments in implementing child protection. In addition, the need to establish a children's forum and Child-Friendly Regency as a form of appreciation in realizing protection and fulfillment of children's rights.

CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
1. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution as a Constitutional foundation has explicitly regulated the importance of protection of Human Rights, including the rights of women and children. In addition to the guarantee from the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the guarantee that every person must have equal dignity and degree has also been recognized internationally. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights or UDHR of 1948 which underlies Human Rights in general has guaranteed that all people are born with freedom, having equal dignity and rights without exception.

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and manage regional government affairs aimed at realizing community welfare through improved services, protection and empowerment of the community. As a community component that plays an important role in realizing a quality generation and as successors to the nation's struggle, women and children must receive guarantees for the fulfillment of children's rights.

To ensure the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in accordance with human dignity and in order to carry out mandatory affairs, regional governments need to provide legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection through the formulation of a policy. The formulation of such policy is a form of support and concrete effort from various other parties in ensuring the fulfillment of the rights of women and children.

The Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is carried out based on the principles of:
a. non-discrimination;
b. the best interests of women and children;
c. the right to life, survival and development; d. respect for children and legal certainty; and
e. local wisdom and justice and gender equality.

The formulation of the Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to:
a. provide guidance in planning and implementing Women's Empowerment and Child Protection policies;
b. increase efforts for Women's Empowerment and fulfillment of children's rights in order to realize improved quality of life for women and children in the Region;
c. increase protection efforts for women and children from actions and policies that violate the rights of women and children; d. increase the value of local wisdom and the role of customs in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, and
e. increase the role of Regional Government and other community institutions in efforts for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation on Women and Child Protection regulates:
a. Improvement of women's quality of life which contains government responsibilities, implementation of PUG, Efforts to increase the role, quality and capacity of women in the political, legal, social and economic fields;
b. Protection of women which contains regional government responsibilities in women's protection, prevention of violence against women, protection for women victims of violence, as well as complaint handling,
c. Child Protection which contains the responsibilities of regional government, parents/family and community in child protection as well as efforts made by regional governments in implementing child protection. In addition, the need to establish a children's forum and Child-Friendly Regency as a form of appreciation in realizing protection and fulfillment of children's rights.

Article 52
(1) Children with disabilities and children with special needs are given equal opportunities to obtain formal, non-formal and informal education services, including inclusive education.
(2) Regional governments provide educators for inclusive education at every education unit.

Article 35
(1) Employers who employ women are obligated to maintain decency, safety and security while in the workplace.
(2) Employers are obligated to place female workers in places that are safe for women's reproductive health.
(3) Employers are obligated to fulfill the rights of female workers to receive wages in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(4) Employers are obligated to provide special breastfeeding facilities at their company.

Article 31
(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services are intended to provide assistance and protection to women victims of acts of violence and sanctions with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and legal certainty.
(2) Types of legal aid services include:
a. legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of official investigation reports;
b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal aid in the examination process at court; d. legal aid in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision; and
e. legal aid in the mediation process.
(3) The Regional Government provides legal aid to women victims of acts of violence based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
(4) In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3), the Regional Government may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other legal assistants who are gender sensitive.

CHAPTER XI
FUNDING
Article 79
Financing for the implementation of programs and activities for women's empowerment and child protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is sourced from:
a. regional revenue and expenditure budget; and
b. other legitimate sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 29
(1) Spiritual guidance as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (2) letter c aims for psychological recovery.
(2) Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented based on the principles of:
a. not imposing any religion or belief; and
b. leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim.
(3) Spiritual guidance is conducted by spiritual guidance officers.
(4) Spiritual guidance officers as referred to in paragraph (3) consist of consultants from the Marriage Advisory, Development and Preservation Board, Officers of the Religious Affairs Office, religious leaders, who possess gender sensitivity or gender awareness.

(1) Every person/entity is prohibited from employing and involving children in the worst forms of work.

(1) Every organizer of an educational unit is obligated to provide opportunities for children to obtain services without discrimination.
